title: Proposal: Improve control over HTML/XML syntax parse errors

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
User agents usually do not implement mechanisms for HTML authors to detect parse errors during the initial document load. In HTML syntax, there are no JavaScript events, DOM nodes, or console messages indicating a parse error. In [XML syntax](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/xhtml.html#the-xhtml-syntax), some user agents insert a parsererror node in the document that can be detected with custom JavaScript that phones home, but only if the parse error occurs after the detection script is parsed. This proposal would specify three new features to the HTML spec:

1. Add support for the [Reporting API](https://wicg.github.io/reporting/) on parse errors, like CSP and HPKP reporting, whether recoverable or not. Multiple parse errors could be aggregated into a single report that is sent once parsing ends, up to some maximum number of errors.
2. Add support for forcing the parse errors to be fatal. This improves security by preventing certain types of [XSS attacks that rely upon malformed markup](https://www.owasp.org/index.php/XSS_Filter_Evasion_Cheat_Sheet#Malformed_IMG_tags), and can help improve error visibility during development.
3. Throw a JavaScript parse error during the main document parsing (the same as during fragment parsing). This would give authors more control to catch and implement their own parse error handling, potentially improving user experience in error scenarios.

These features would assist authors during development and live operations and reduce the need for out-of-band conformance checking. Standalone conformance checkers (validators) are problematic due to inconsistencies with actual browser parser implementations, the impracticality of performing conformance checks against all URLs and states in a web application, and the overhead of maintaining syntax a conformance checker as part of QA and CI processes.

The strictness of the XML syntax of HTML is valuable for catching syntax bugs (like potential XSS vectors), but it is an unattractive option if authors want the parser to use the [error handling described in the spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parse-errors). Using XML syntax might be more popular if @annevk's [XML5 spec](https://github.com/annevk/xml5) with non-fatal parsing error handling was implemented, but XML syntax authors would still need to deal with the trivial incompatibilities with HTML syntax either way, like nodeName capitalization differences.

**Example headers:**

Force parse errors to be fatal, and show a parsererror node:

    HTML-Parse-Error: show-error

Treat parse errors are non-fatal whenever possible, send a report on errors encountered during parsing, and do not show a parseerror node:

    HTML-Parse-Error-Report-Only: report-to parse-error-endpoint

**Summary of current and proposed parse error behavior:**

| | current text/html | current application/xhtml+xml | proposed text/html | proposed application/xhtml+xml |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **fatal** | no | yes | optional | yes |
| **JS error** | no | no | yes | yes |
| **inject parsererror** | no | some UAs | optional | optional |
| **reporting API** | no | no | optional | optional |

There's room to expand on this idea to do things like allowing opt-in to stricter syntax under HTML syntax that removes the idiosyncrasies that set it apart from XML syntax, or including/excluding specific types of parse errors from reporting, defining meta tag support, etc., but those aren't the main focus here.

Thoughts?
